narr: A training line of thunderstorms occurred just west of South Boston, producing between three and four inches of rainfall within a span of three hours. Rainfall rates at times were observed to be in excess of 3.5 inches per hour. Runoff from this rainfall collected in Poplar Creek, causing the creek to rise out of its banks in the town of South Boston, resulting in flooding of roads near the Dan River. FLASH data did not appear impressive with this event, indicating a maximum 1-hou ARI of between a 10-year and a 20-year event. The 1-hour QPE/FFG ration maxed out at 1.0, and CREST Unit Streamflow was marginal, between 90 and 180 cfs/mi^2.
ev: Heavy rainfall from a training thunderstorm caused Poplar Crek to overflow its banks and flood several inches deep across portions of Railroad Avenue, Summit Drive, and Edmonds Street.
lsr: High water was reported over Railroad Avenue and Summit Drive as well as Edmunds Street and Summit Drive. This was likely due to flooding from Poplar Creek. Time estimated from National Water Model.
